text:
sarah: Hey support — customer `acme-inc` is seeing a big spike of 502/504s on Hosted API when they run large embedding batches. Started ~10:12 UTC, now 10:28. Example client trace id: `trace-93a2f`. They say it repros reliably when splitting into 1200-item batches.

mike: Can you paste the curl/logs? any error body from edge?

sarah: quick curl they used:```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-xl","input": ["...1200 items..."]}'
```They get `HTTP/2 502` or long tail `504` after ~12s. No body sometimes.

jenny: @mike @alejandro tagging eng-sre in case this is connection-pool/keepalive exhaustion again. What region?

sarah: eu-west-1. Traffic pattern: single host doing back-to-back batches (no client concurrency but big request body). We see spike in edge queue depth on dashboards: https://grafana/redwood/edge/qdepth?panelId=7 (link from customer logs).

alejandro: Thanks. Can you grab the edge trace headers (x-request-id, x-edge-node) from the failed responses? Also any ingress logs with upstream response times?

sarah: i have one failed header dump: `x-request-id: rq-84b1`, `x-edge-node: eu1-edge-17`, `x-forwarded-for: 34.89.12.45`. Upstream shows `upstream_response_time` ~0.03s then connection reset.

mike: upstream small time then reset suggests NGINX/Envoy early-close while proxy still reading client body -> possible request body large + backpressure on upstream, or upstream closed conn due to header size/timeout. Do we have ingress timeouts set for large bodies?

alejandro: On Hosted API we have `client_body_timeout` 60s default; but keepalive pool per node is limited. Large single-request payloads can block worker, causing conn queueing. Repro plan: try smaller batches (<=500) and/or chunk streaming.

sarah: Customer already tried 500 and saw success. They said 800 produced intermittent 502. So threshold ~600-700.

kevin: Quick mitigation: suggest customer switch to chunked/batched streaming (client-side chunking) or use Dedicated if they need big single-shot batches. I'll patch support KB with that.

mike: Also let's check edge h2 keepalive pools and midproxy. @oncall-bot can you run a query for `edge.h2.pool.available` around 10:00-10:40 eu-west-1?

oncall-bot: Query submitted: metrics `edge.h2.pool.available` for eu-west-1 between 2026-03-18T10:00:00Z and 2026-03-18T10:40:00Z. Returning: sudden drop from 128 -> 6 at 10:12, recovered ~10:33.

alejandro: That matches. Looks like pool exhaustion during big uploads causing queue spikes and proxy resets. Root cause likely long-lived request bodies occupying h2 streams.

jenny: Action items: (1) Recommend client chunking / reduce batch size (contact customer with repro steps) — OWNER: sarah. (2) Investigate edge keepalive pool sizing and h2 stream eviction logic — OWNER: alejandro. (3) Add a short-term rule to detect large single-request body patterns and auto-suggest chunking in support console — OWNER: kevin.

sarah: I messaged customer with steps: split into 400-item batches OR use streaming (example snippet). They confirmed reduced errors after switching to 400.

alejandro: From infra side I'll look at changing pool_target and add telemetry to count large-body single-shot requests. Will check if we can increase concurrency without regressing memory.

mike: Also add a clear error message when we detect `client body size causing pool exhaustion` so customers don't assume unrelated upstream errors.

kevin: Noted. I'll add KB article and email template.

jenny: Nice triage. Leaving this thread open until infra PR lands. Marking P2.

sarah: Closing for now — customer back on 400-batches, no errors for 30m. We'll reopen if anything. :white_check_mark:
